title: Inter-Annotator Agreement Study on Safety Benchmark Ground Truth
original_idea: Re-annotate a sample of 200-300 AILuminate public prompts with three to five independent raters. Compute inter-rater agreement and compare to benchmark's reported label confidence.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Foundational question: if ground truth labels lack consensus, all downstream evaluations are compromised. Important prior-layer validity issue.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Statistical methods (inter-rater agreement) are standard. However, recruiting and coordinating 3-5 independent raters adds logistical complexity beyond pure coding work. Annotation guidelines need careful design.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Recruiting raters, designing annotation guidelines, managing annotation process, computing agreement statistics. Human coordination overhead makes this broader than it appears.

novelty.reasoning: Inter-annotator agreement (IAA) is well-studied in NLP generally. 'Counting on Consensus: Selecting the Right Inter-annotator Agreement Metric for NLP' (arXiv:2603.06865, 2026) provides comprehensive methodology. The importance of IAA for benchmark reliability is recognized — low consensus in ground truth labels undermines all downstream evaluations. However, a specific re-annotation study targeting AILuminate public prompts with independent raters and comparison to benchmark-reported label confidence has not been published. The AILuminate methodology documentation does describe their annotation process but independent replication studies are absent. The idea provides a concrete empirical contribution, though the methodology is standard.

AILuminate public prompts.details: Confirmed: MLCommons released AILuminate CC DEMO benchmark prompt dataset to GitHub (Jan 2025). Public prompts available for re-annotation.

Inter-rater agreement methodology.details: Standard methodology (Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, Krippendorff's alpha). Well-established in annotation literature.
